subject: gamers
one_liner: A card reader that clips to your monitor, so the people in your house finally pay for what they use.
brand_voice_notes: Hardware launch gravity applied to sibling disputes. Speaks like a payments company that has read too many Discord arguments. Never says 'gamer' with a wink. Fees are disclosed promptly and with pride. Every household relationship is treated as an accounts-receivable problem.

hero.h1: Your setup is a small business. Start invoicing like one.
hero.sub: Hotbar mounts to your monitor bezel and charges siblings, roommates, and partners for every controller, couch seat, and carry they consume. Funds settle in 2 business days or one ranked match, whichever ends first.

features.title: Controller rental, metered by the minute
features.blurb: Player 2 is billed from the moment the light turns blue. A drift surcharge applies automatically if they flick the stick near the vents.

features.title: Tap to spectate
features.blurb: Anyone who stands behind your chair for more than 40 seconds is presented with the reader. Commentary is billed separately at the advice rate.

features.title: Carry invoicing
features.blurb: Getting your cousin through a raid used to be a favor. Hotbar itemizes every revive, every boss pull, every 'just stand there,' and emails a PDF to his mom.

pricing_tiers.name: Solo Queue
pricing_tiers.tagline: 2.9% + 30¢ per tap. Same as everyone else.
perks: Tip screen with 18%, 20%, and GG presets
Receipts printed in a font that looks expensive

pricing_tiers.name: Duo
pricing_tiers.tagline: For households with exactly one other person who keeps asking.
perks: Two readers, one for the couch arm
Snack-run surcharge on any order placed mid-match

pricing_tiers.name: Clan
pricing_tiers.tagline: For LAN parties, dorm floors, and one man named Derek with nine monitors.
perks: Seat pricing by distance from the TV

testimonials.quote: My brother owed me $412 in controller time. I didn't know that until Hotbar told me. Now he knows too.
testimonials.name: Priya Venkataraman
testimonials.title: Diamond II Support Main, Head of Household Receivables

testimonials.quote: I put the second reader on the mini fridge. Energy drink theft is down 80 percent. My roommate moved out, which is also down.
testimonials.name: Colt Brannigan
testimonials.title: Apartment 4C Operations Lead, Part-Time Sniper

testimonials.quote: The tip screen asked my dad for 20% after he brought me a sandwich. He tipped. We have not discussed it.
testimonials.name: Mara Okonkwo-Beale
testimonials.title: Speedrunner (Any%, Unverified), Age 16

demo_screen_concept: Hotbar Register: a dark point-of-sale checkout screen. Left side is a grid of tappable item tiles filtered by category tabs (Hardware, Seating, Services, Pantry): 'Controller rental, 1 hr', 'Couch seat, left (the good one)', 'Carried through raid', 'Silence during ranked', 'Headset loan, mic muted'. Right side is a running ticket with quantity steppers, a customer picker (Jayden, younger brother; Mom; Theo, roommate) showing each customer's outstanding balance, a tip selector with 18% / 20% / GG / No tip (greyed out, 'unavailable in your region'), and a Charge button that runs a tap animation and opens a thermal-receipt modal.

design_direction.style: Hardware-launch corridor, matte peripheral dark mode. One rationed lime accent used only for live/charge states, like a status LED on a black desk; everything else is graphite, hairline spec rules, and big product photography.
design_direction.archetype: Consumer hardware launch page (Square Reader / peripheral product page): full-bleed hero shot, spec strip, feature corridor threaded by a vertical spine, pricing as SKU cards.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Status-LED pulse on the lime accent, a slow 'tap' ripple on the CTA, spine line that draws as sections enter. All transform/opacity, disabled under reduced motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-bleed photograph of the reader on a dark desk with lime underglow; headline bottom-left in Russo One, spec strip below (weight, latency, fee) in tabular Chakra Petch. Single lime CTA.

images.rationale: Hardware-launch archetype calls for a full-bleed product shot, so the hero gets 1 image. Demo is a POS register (tiles, ticket, receipt), which is UI- and type-shaped, so no demo assets. Remaining 3 of budget go to testimonial headshots.
